body:
# id(world/replication): `SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign` signs envelopes every receiver rejects — version, header version, payload digest, cursor chain, terminal and snapshot-base rules are never checked

## Summary

`SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign` (`pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs:495`) is the production signing entry point for replication frames (used by `world_replication_net.rs:320` `write_envelope`, the writer feed). It refuses only two things:

- the signing key not matching the envelope's claimed `source`, and
- a payload longer than `MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES`.

Every other rule that `ReplicationTracker::accept` (same file, `:744ff`) enforces **before** a frame may advance a replica is unchecked at signing time, and several of those rules are decidable from the envelope alone (no receiver/session state needed). A hand-built `ReplicationEnvelope` (all fields are `pub`, and `tail`/`snapshot`/`terminal` are not the only way to build one) therefore signs `Ok`/`Some` and is then rejected by **every** receiver, unconditionally:

| # | Signed shape | `sign()` | Every `accept()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `version = 99` | `Some` | `UnsupportedEnvelopeVersion(99)` |
| 2 | `header_version = 0` or `MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION + 1` | `Some` | `UnsupportedJournalVersion(..)` |
| 3 | `payload_digest != payload_digest(payload)` | `Some` | `PayloadDigestMismatch` |
| 4 | `cursor_after != chain_payload(cursor_before, payload)` | `Some` | `EntryChainMismatch` |
| 5 | payload not complete decodable journal entries | `Some` | `MalformedPayload` |
| 6 | `Terminal` with a non-empty payload (or `cursor_before != cursor_after`) | `Some` | `TerminalCursorMismatch` |
| 7 | `Snapshot` with `cursor_before != chain_base_cursor(world_id, source, header_version)` | `Some` | `CursorFork` |
| 8 | Snapshot/tail payload whose journal header does not match the envelope (wrong world/version, duplicate `Created`) | `Some` | `InvalidJournalHeader` (#4486 rule) |

This is the same dead-on-arrival signing pattern as the earlier `sign_*` filings in this crate (e.g. #6422 currency, #6434 match_audit, #6447 `sign_move`): the signer is the writer itself, so a frame signed this way is not an attacker's forgery the receiver heroically stops — it is this node's own output that no peer can ever accept, discovered only when a sync session fails frame-by-frame.

## Evidence

Verified this run on the laptop primary at `6271e067012c360e108fa658ae23b5d9dedf6867` with a probe integration test against the real `id` crate (`~/git/fleet/probe-replication-sign/pkgs/id/tests/probe_replication_sign.rs`, worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-replication-sign`):

- Control: a `ReplicationEnvelope::tail(..)` envelope signs and a fresh `ReplicationTracker` accepts it.
- Cases 1–8 above: each mutated/hand-built envelope's `sign()` returned `Some`, `verify_signature()` passes (the signature is genuinely valid), and a fresh tracker's `accept()` returned exactly the named error in the table. 1 test passed.

Code read confirming the gap:

- `replication.rs:495-508` — `sign()` checks only `source` and payload length, then signs `signing_bytes()`.
- `replication.rs:744-830` — `accept()` checks envelope version, journal header version range (`JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION`), payload digest equality, `chain_payload(cursor_before, payload) == cursor_after`, the snapshot base cursor, the terminal shape, and `validate_payload_journal_header` — none of which `sign()` mirrors.
- The safe constructors (`tail` :257, `snapshot` :287, `terminal` :313) compute digest/cursors correctly, which is why production frames are fine today — the hole is that `sign()` will sign anything else, and its doc comment ("refusing to sign for a key that is not the envelope's claimed source, and refusing an over-bound payload") presents those two as the refusal contract.
- Precedent that a refusing signer is workable: `replication_receiver.rs:626` tests already contain `sign_unbounded`, a helper that replicates the signing-bytes contract precisely because "the production signer refuses to sign" an over-bound payload. Receiver tests that need a lying signer can use the same bypass technique for the newly refused shapes (the `SignedReplicationEnvelope` fields are `pub`).

Not in scope (receiver-state-dependent, cannot be decided at signing time): world/pinned-source matching, session nonce, `prev_frame_digest` chaining, tail cursor gap/fork vs the receiver's current cursor. Those stay receiver-only.

## Why it matters

Replication is the read-replica path for worlds (#806). A writer that signs an always-rejected frame wastes a sync session and surfaces as an opaque peer-side refusal, far from the construction site that caused it. Every other signing path in this crate that gained a "refuse here what receipt would refuse" check (e.g. `directory::declare_home` #3187, `sign_after` symmetry #5623) did so to move exactly this class of failure to the moment of signing, with the rule named.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign` returns `None` for an envelope that fails any envelope-local rule `accept()` enforces: envelope version, journal header version range, payload-digest equality, payload chaining to `cursor_after` (including malformed payload), snapshot base cursor, terminal shape (empty payload, `cursor_before == cursor_after`), and payload journal-header agreement (#4486).
- [ ] A valid `tail`/`snapshot`/`terminal` constructor envelope still signs `Some` and is accepted by a fresh tracker (existing replication tests keep passing).
- [ ] Tests pin each refused shape at the signer, and receiver tests that intentionally sign lying envelopes construct them via a direct/bypass helper (as `sign_unbounded` already does), not via the production `sign()`.
- [ ] The `sign()` doc comment states the full refusal contract.

## Dedup

Searched open and closed issues for `SignedReplicationEnvelope`, "replication envelope", "replication sign" (2026-11-06): only #806 (the F12.13 feature epic) and closed #4966 (checkpoint splitting) — neither covers signer-side validation. Distinct from #6447 (`sign_move` world-core domain) — different module, different signed type, different receiver rules.
